note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. A consensus national toss-up. Ballotpedia lists three qualified unaffiliated/independent general-election candidates (Alcorn, Rich, Evans), not curated here.

ME-senate.statusNote: Sen. Susan Collins (R), Senate Appropriations chair, faces former state Senate President Troy Jackson (D). Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary with 72% but withdrew on July 10; the Maine Democratic Party nominated Jackson on July 25 and the Secretary of State lists him as the replacement candidate. Rated a toss-up by the Cook Political Report. Jackson's positions are not researched yet.

ME-house-1.statusNote: Rep. Chellie Pingree (D) was unopposed in the June 9, 2026 primary and faces Republican Ron Russell. Maine runs both the primary and the general with ranked choice voting. We know who's running, positions not researched yet.

ME-house-2.statusNote: Open seat: Rep. Jared Golden (D) announced in November 2025 that he would not seek reelection. Former Secretary of State Matt Dunlap won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary in a ranked choice runoff, 52.5% to 47.5% over Joe Baldacci, and faces former Gov. Paul LePage (R). We know who's running, positions not researched yet.

candidates.name: Susan Collins
candidates.now: U.S. Senator; Chair, Senate Appropriations Committee
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 1997, seeking a sixth term; chairs the Appropriations Committee and holds the longest perfect attendance streak in Senate history. From a sixth-generation Caribou lumber family. Repeatedly ranked the Senate's most bipartisan member; voted to convict President Trump in the 2021 impeachment trial.
priorities: Health care: Alzheimer's, diabetes, rural access

cost.label: Record: champions federal home-heating assistance; secured $4B in LIHEAP funding and pressed for its release (Senate office)

health.label: One of the Republican votes that blocked repealing the ACA without replacement in 2017; co-sponsored insulin and drug-price bills (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Record: directs federal affordable-housing funding to Maine as an appropriator (Senate office)

immigration.label: Voted for the 2013 comprehensive reform with a citizenship path; opposed family separation and the 2017 travel ban (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act after securing SALT and medical-expense amendments (Senate office)

climate.label: Backs offshore wind expansion; co-authored a 30% offshore-wind investment tax credit (Senate office)

education.label: Voted against Betsy DeVos for Education Secretary, citing commitment to public and rural schools (Senate office)

repro.label: Self-identified pro-choice: opposed 20-week bans and Planned Parenthood defunding, but voted to confirm Justice Kavanaugh (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Mixed: backs Electoral Count Act reform to stop Congress overriding state election results, but joined the GOP in blocking the Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act in Jan 2022, calling it 'a federal takeover of state elections' (Maine Public)

safety.label: Voted yes on the First Step Act of 2018, the 87-12 sentencing-reform and prison-reentry law (Senate roll call 271)

controversies.label: Her Kavanaugh vote, cast after predicting he would not overturn Roe, was contradicted by the Dobbs decision (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Graham Platner
candidates.background: Oyster farmer, Marine Corps and Army National Guard veteran (Iraq and Afghanistan), and political newcomer endorsed by Bernie Sanders. Won the June Democratic primary over Gov. Janet Mills, who had suspended her campaign in April. His campaign rejects PAC money and reported a $4.1M first-quarter 2026 haul, largely from working people.
priorities: Get billionaire money out of politics

cost.label: Raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation; 'cost-of-living tax cut' for working people (campaign platform)

health.label: Medicare for All, replacing for-profit insurance; Medicare drug-price negotiation (campaign platform)

housing.label: Restore federal housing investment, expand VA home loans, ban hedge funds from buying homes (campaign platform)

immigration.label: Opposes mass deportation; reform pairing strong border security with a path to citizenship (campaign platform)

taxes.label: Billionaire minimum tax; lift the Social Security payroll-tax cap (campaign platform)

climate.label: Urgent climate action; defend and strengthen Clean Air and Clean Water Act enforcement (campaign platform)

education.label: Opposes private-school vouchers; federal investment so every public district is adequately funded (campaign platform)

safety.label: Legalize cannabis with clemency for drug-war convictions; invest revenue in addiction treatment and prevention (campaign platform)

repro.label: Strong federal statutory guarantee of the right to choose (campaign platform)

controversies.label: A 2007 tattoo compared to the Nazi Totenkopf ('I never once thought about it in that context'), covered up once flagged, and offensive Reddit posts he admits were angry and crude, citing post-infantry trauma (WGME)
